# AdChanger

> AdChanger is a Mac app that shows one small, still ad in the macOS menu bar, next to the clock, and pays the person
> who shows it for every verified minute. Businesses use the same app to build the ad, choose who sees it and pay
> only for verified minutes. Its first product is MacAd, the menu-bar ad. AdChanger is a bootstrapped startup
> founded in September 2026 by Yiğit Ali Kurt; contact yigit@adchanger.net. Status: pre-launch (the native Mac app and
> serving foundation are working; the public download is not live yet; join the waitlist by email).

## Key facts

- Earning: a Mac user keeps 65% of every verified minute: £2.60 / €3.25 / $3.90 per 1,000 minutes (£0.0026 a minute in pounds). An 8-hour working day with an ad running throughout is about £1.25. One person counts for at most 1,000 minutes of one ad a day. Nothing is paid for an idle, locked or sleeping Mac.
- A verified minute: the whole ad on screen for 60 seconds while the Mac is awake and in use. The server checks every minute and accepts it once.
- Advertising: businesses pay £4 / €5 / $6 per 1,000 verified minutes, from prepaid credit; nothing for unfinished or paused minutes; never more than the budget. A person reviews every ad.
- Payouts: through Whop, from 10 in the earner's currency, after a 3-day hold. AdChanger never sees card or bank details.
- Privacy and safety: the app never sees the screen, keystrokes, microphone, camera, app contents or browsing history, and asks for no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission. The ad can be paused, snoozed or stopped at any time. Data is stored in London (Supabase).
- Platform: macOS 12 or later. AdChanger is for people 18 or older, earners and advertisers alike. UK first, available worldwide.

# Earn money from your Mac with one small ad in the menu bar

Source: https://adchanger.net/earn-money-on-mac (updated 2026-10-06)

AdChanger is a Mac app that shows one small, still ad in your menu bar, next to the clock, and pays you for every minute it is seen while you use your Mac. Advertisers pay £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 verified minutes and you keep 65%: £2.60 per 1,000 minutes in pounds.

## How it works

MacAd, the product inside the AdChanger app, puts one ad in your menu bar. There are no pop-ups, no sound and no window to keep open.

- Step 1: Install AdChanger on a Mac running macOS 12 or later and sign in with an email link, Google or GitHub.
- Step 2: Tell the app your age band and, if you wish, what you do on your Mac, your interests and what you plan to buy. These answers are optional.
- Step 3: The bar appears in your menu bar, next to the clock, and shows one ad at a time.
- Step 4: Each time the whole ad has been on screen for 60 seconds while your Mac is awake and in use, AdChanger's server counts one verified minute.
- Step 5: Your share of each minute is added to your balance, waits 3 days, and can then be withdrawn through Whop.

If you are away from your Mac for 8 minutes, the clock waits. If the Mac locks, sleeps or shuts down, or you pause, snooze or stop the bar, the unfinished minute does not count.

When no ad fits you well enough, or during a short break between paid stretches, the bar shows AdChanger's own message instead. Those minutes earn nothing.

## What a minute is worth

The price of a minute is published and fixed per currency. You keep 65% of it; AdChanger keeps the rest.

- GBP: the advertiser pays £0.004 a minute (£4 per 1,000); you keep £0.0026 a minute, which is £2.60 per 1,000 minutes.
- EUR: the advertiser pays €0.005 a minute (€5 per 1,000); you keep €0.00325 a minute, which is €3.25 per 1,000 minutes.
- USD: the advertiser pays $0.006 a minute ($6 per 1,000); you keep $0.0039 a minute, which is $3.90 per 1,000 minutes.

If you joined with someone's affiliate code, you keep 70% instead (£2.80 per 1,000 minutes in pounds). The price the advertiser pays does not change.

An ad only shows in the countries its advertiser chose, so what is on offer depends on where you are.

## A worked example

This is an example, not a promise. Suppose an ad runs for a full 8-hour working day (480 minutes) while you are at your Mac and using it:

- GBP: about £1.25 a day, or roughly £37 over 30 such days.
- EUR: about €1.56 a day, or roughly €47 over 30 such days.
- USD: about $1.87 a day, or roughly $56 over 30 such days.

One person is counted for at most 1,000 minutes of the same ad a day (16 h 40 min), so one ad can pay you at most £2.60, €3.25 or $3.90 in a day.

What you actually earn depends on the ads running for your country and on how long your Mac is awake and in use. AdChanger does not pay for a Mac that is idle, locked, asleep or left unattended, and it promises no fixed amount.

## Getting paid

- Each minute's earnings wait 3 days so invalid activity can be checked, then become available.
- You can withdraw available earnings from £10, €10 or $10 upwards, one withdrawal at a time.
- Payouts go through Whop. You link a Whop account once, and Whop checks your ID before it pays out.
- From Whop you send the money to your bank or card. Whop's own terms and fees apply to that step.
- AdChanger never sees or stores your bank or card details; Whop holds them.
- You are responsible for any tax on what you earn.

Whop is the only payment route today. Stripe, Wise and PayPal are planned.

## What it needs from you

- A Mac with macOS 12 Monterey or later.
- Room in the menu bar for one bar, 180 points wide. If the menu bar is too full, the app tells you, and nothing counts until there is room.
- You must be 18 or over.
- One account per person. Only one of your Macs earns at a time.

Your answers are what advertisers pay for. You can switch them off in Settings at any time; while they are off, you see no ads and earn nothing.

## What it never does

To count a minute, the app only checks that the ad is on screen and that your Mac is awake and in use. It never sees:

- your screen, screenshots or recordings (it asks for no Screen Recording permission);
- what you type (it asks for no Accessibility permission);
- your microphone or camera;
- what is inside your apps, documents or messages;
- your browsing or search history.

To pick a fitting ad, it checks which app is in front, such as a coding or design tool. The name of that app never leaves your Mac, and you can switch this off in Settings.

The full details are on [Is AdChanger safe?](https://adchanger.net/safety) and in the [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy).

## How it compares with other ways to earn from a Mac

Apps that pay you on a Mac generally pay for one of four things. Each is a fair trade if you know which one you are making.

- Surveys and micro-tasks pay for your active time: you earn while you answer or click, and stop when you stop.
- Bandwidth-sharing apps pay for your internet connection, which other parties route traffic through.
- Compute or mining apps pay for your processor and electricity.
- AdChanger pays for a small area of your menu bar while you work: one still ad, counted only while you are using your Mac. It does not share your connection or use your processor for mining.

AdChanger asks for no extra effort once it is running. In exchange, its earnings are tied to the hours you are at your Mac, and the rate per minute is small.

## Is it worth it?

For most people the honest answer is: a small, steady extra. At £2.60 per 1,000 minutes, the amount grows with the hours you spend at your Mac, not with anything extra you do.

It suits people who are at a Mac for many hours a day, such as developers, designers, writers, students and people running a business from their laptop. It is not a way to earn while you are away.

You can stop at any time, so the simplest test is to run it for a few weeks and look at the Dashboard, which shows your earnings by day, week, month and year.

## Join the waitlist

AdChanger has not launched yet: the Mac app is being built and the download is not public yet. Features, including payouts, may not all be switched on at first.

To join the waitlist, email yigit@adchanger.net with the subject "Waitlist". You get an email when the download is ready, and it will be on the [home page](https://adchanger.net/) the same day.

## Questions about earning

### Can I really get paid to show ads on my Mac?

Yes. AdChanger shows one small ad in your Mac's menu bar and pays you 65% of what the advertiser pays for each verified minute, which is £2.60, €3.25 or $3.90 per 1,000 minutes. The download is not public yet.

### How much can I earn per day or per month?

As an example, an 8-hour day with an ad running the whole time comes to about £1.25, or roughly £37 over 30 such days. One ad can pay you at most £2.60 a day. Real earnings depend on the ads running in your country and how long your Mac is in use; no amount is promised.

### Does AdChanger pay when my Mac is idle?

No. A minute only counts while the Mac is awake and in use. If you are away for 8 minutes the clock waits, and if the Mac locks or sleeps the unfinished minute does not count.

### Is AdChanger a scam?

AdChanger publishes who runs it (its founder, Yiğit Ali Kurt), a contact address (yigit@adchanger.net), its prices and revenue split, its [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms) and its [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy). It never sees your bank details, pays out through Whop, and the terms set out no charge for earning. It has not launched yet, which it states openly.

### What do I need to start earning with AdChanger?

A Mac with macOS 12 or later, room for one bar in the menu bar, and an age of 18 or over. To be paid, you also need a Whop account, which checks your ID once.

### Can I earn from AdChanger outside the UK?

Yes. Anyone with a Mac, in any country, can earn. An ad only shows in the countries its advertiser chose, so how many paid ads you see depends on where you are. The UK is AdChanger's first market.

### Can I pause AdChanger?

Yes. Click the bar to pause, snooze (for 1 hour, 3 hours or until tomorrow) or stop it. Minutes only count while it is running.

# Advertise in the Mac menu bar

Source: https://adchanger.net/advertise (updated 2026-10-07)

MacAd puts your brand in the Mac menu bar, next to the clock, and you pay only for verified minutes: £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000, depending on your currency. A minute counts only after your whole ad has been on screen for 60 seconds while someone is using their Mac.

## The placement

MacAd is one ad per Mac, in the menu bar, beside the clock and the system icons. It sits outside the windows people work in, so it never covers what they are doing.

- Size on screen: 180 × 34 points, a rounded rectangle.
- File: a still PNG at 720 × 136 pixels (or 360 × 68), up to 10 MB. No animation.
- Text: a brand name of up to 12 characters and a short line of up to 42, matching the words in the image.
- Link: a secure https:// page of your choice, opened when someone clicks the bar.
- It is shown on light and dark menu bars, and the app previews both before you submit.

The people who see it chose to install AdChanger and are paid for the minutes your ad is on screen, so the bar is welcome rather than forced on them.

## How you pay

You pay per verified minute, and for nothing else. The price is published and the same for every advertiser:

- GBP: £0.004 per verified minute, £4 per 1,000.
- EUR: €0.005 per verified minute, €5 per 1,000.
- USD: $0.006 per verified minute, $6 per 1,000.

Of every minute, 65% goes to the person whose Mac shows your ad and 35% to AdChanger.

- Your billing country, set once, fixes your currency: pounds in the UK, euros in the EU, dollars everywhere else.
- You add credit through Whop before a campaign runs, in payments of 10 to 10,000 in your currency. Whop takes the card; AdChanger never sees it.
- A campaign's budget is set aside from your credit in full before it starts and is spent one verified minute at a time.
- When the budget runs out, the bar stops. You are never charged more than your budget.
- You pay nothing for unfinished minutes, idle or locked screens, or while a person has paused, snoozed or stopped the bar.
- Budget you do not spend returns to your credit for the next campaign. Credit is not paid back in cash; the one exception is a payment for an ad that was rejected before a single minute ran.

## Targeting

MacAd's targeting is built on what people choose to tell AdChanger and on what they are doing at that moment, not on tracking them across apps or websites.

- Places: any country in the world, regions or worldwide, with optional cities. A city is only used where enough people live there to keep them anonymous.
- The moment: the app in front of the person right now, such as Xcode or Figma. The app's name never leaves their Mac; only the match is used.
- What they do on their Mac: code, design, music and video, writing, running a business, money, study or games, and what they need, such as "first customers" or "exams".
- Interests: topics people picked themselves.
- Buying plans and life moments: a new Mac, moving house, a new job. Plans count less after 60 days and stop counting after 120.

While you plan a campaign, the app shows a rounded estimate of how many people fit, never the people themselves.

Targeting is only as precise as people's answers, and answers are optional. If nothing fits a person well enough, no paid bar shows, so you do not pay for filler. A bar someone has seen for hours gives way to another, so attention stays fresh.

## Measurement

Every campaign reports verified minutes and spend, then each step people take:

- Seen: people whose Mac showed your bar for verified minutes.
- Noticed: people whose pointer rested on the bar.
- Clicked: people who clicked through to your page.
- Reached your page and became customers: measured with the click ID added to your link (as mac=) and the sales your website or shop reports.

To report those steps, add the AdChanger tag to your website, or send sales from your server. How, and what it collects, is on [Measure sales](https://adchanger.net/measure).

A sale counts for your ad when it happens within 7 days of a click on it. If your bar carries a discount code, the app copies it for the person when they open the bar, and you must honour it.

Results by place and time are grouped: any group of fewer than 5 people is merged into "other". You never receive a list of people, names or emails.

## Review and rules

A person reviews every ad, its link and the page it opens before it runs, and tells you why if it is not approved. A change to an approved ad is reviewed again.

AdChanger does not accept ads for:

- gambling or betting;
- adult sexual content or services;
- prescription medicines;
- politics or elections;
- speculative crypto or token investments.

Everyone who sees your bar is 18 or over. Sensitive subjects, such as alcohol or dating, get a closer look in review.

You must be 18 or over, be allowed to act for the business, and have the right to every word, logo and image in your ad. The full rules are in the [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms).

## Building the ad

You build the ad inside the AdChanger app, with a live preview at real size. You can place it in your own menu bar to see exactly how it looks next to the clock.

No designer is needed. The app gives you instructions to copy into an image-making AI, together with your logo and photos. The AI's image is usually wider than the bar; the app trims the empty border and cuts the bar from its middle at the exact size.

The advertiser pages in the app open only after Touch ID or your Mac's password, and each member of your team can be given their own role.

## Getting started

AdChanger has not launched yet, and the UK is its first market; advertisers can run ads anywhere in the world.

To join the waitlist, email yigit@adchanger.net with the subject "Waitlist: advertising", your business name and website. The Mac app is being built and its download is not public yet; you get an email when it is ready.

How the earner side works is on [Earn on your Mac](https://adchanger.net/earn-money-on-mac); how the app handles people's data is on [Is AdChanger safe?](https://adchanger.net/safety).

## Questions from advertisers

### How much does a MacAd campaign cost?

You set the budget. MacAd charges £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 verified minutes, depending on your billing currency, and stops when the budget is used. Each payment is between 10 and 10,000 in your currency.

### What counts as a verified minute for advertisers?

A minute counts after your whole ad has been on screen for 60 seconds while the Mac is awake and in use. Idle, locked and sleeping Macs are never billed, and AdChanger's server accepts each minute once.

### Can I get a refund on MacAd credit?

Unspent budget returns to your credit for your next campaign, but credit is not paid back in cash. If AdChanger rejects your ad and not one minute of it ran, that payment is refunded. Your rights under law are not affected.

### What size is a MacAd image?

A still PNG of 720 × 136 pixels (or 360 × 68), up to 10 MB, shown at 180 × 34 points in the menu bar. If you make it with an image AI, the app cuts the bar from a wider image for you.

### Can I target a city with MacAd?

Yes, cities are optional on top of countries. A city is only used where enough people live there to keep them anonymous, and results for groups under 5 people are merged.

### How long does MacAd count a sale after a click?

7 days. A sale counts for your ad when it happens within 7 days of a click on it, measured with the click ID on your link and the sales your website or shop reports ([Measure sales](https://adchanger.net/measure)).

# Measure sales from MacAd

Source: https://adchanger.net/measure (updated 2026-10-07)

The AdChanger tag tells AdChanger what happens on your website after someone clicks your MacAd bar: they arrived, stayed, looked around, added to cart or bought. A sale counts for your ad when it happens within 7 days of the last click on it.

## How it works

When someone clicks your bar, the AdChanger app opens your link with a click ID added to it, for example ?mac=k3x9q2m7v4p8z1aa. The tag on your page reads that ID and reports what the visitor does, so the results in the app can show which clicks became customers.

- Visitors who did not arrive from a MacAd click are ignored: without a click ID the tag sends nothing.
- The tag loads without holding up your page, adds no visible element and never lets an error of its own reach your page.
- If a visitor clicks your bar more than once, the most recent click gets the credit.

## Paste the tag

Put these lines in the <head> of every page of your website, or add them through your tag manager. Replace pk_your_key with your site key: in the AdChanger app, open Advertise, then Measure sales.

```html
<script>
  window.adchanger = window.adchanger || function () { (adchanger.q = adchanger.q || []).push(arguments); };
</script>
<script async src="https://adchanger.net/tag.js" data-key="pk_your_key"></script>
```

The site key starts with pk_ and is made to sit in your page's code: it can only report events, and it cannot read your results. The first line lets you call adchanger() before the tag has finished loading; those calls are sent once it has.

With only these lines in place, the tag reports three things on its own:

- Arrived: the visitor reached your page from a MacAd click.
- Stayed 30 seconds: your page was on screen for 30 seconds (time in a background tab does not count).
- Looked around: the visitor scrolled at least half-way down the page, or opened a second page of your site.

If your site uses a Content Security Policy, allow https://adchanger.net/tag.js as a script source and https://adidmymsbpzrumtytsmg.supabase.co/functions/v1/measure/event as a connect source.

## Mark add-to-cart and purchases

Call these where they happen: the first when something is added to the cart, the second on the page that confirms a finished order.

```js
adchanger("add_to_cart");

adchanger("purchase", { order_id: "order-1234", value: 49.99, currency: "GBP" });
```

- order_id: your own order number, up to 128 characters, so that AdChanger can tell one order from another and count each order once.
- value: the order total in ordinary units, such as 49.99. It is sent as minor units (4999).
- currency: GBP, USD or EUR. With any other currency the sale is still counted, without its value.

Send no names, email addresses or other details about the customer: the tag accepts only these three fields and drops anything else.

## Shopify

Paste the tag into your theme (Online Store, Themes, Edit code, theme.liquid, inside <head>) so visits are measured.

Shopify does not run ordinary scripts on its checkout and order status pages. It runs custom pixels there instead, in a separate frame where the tag cannot see your shop's address. To report the sale there, add a custom pixel under Settings, Customer events, with the code below, and set its customer privacy permission to match your consent banner. It reads the click ID that the tag stored (so it reports sales only from visitors who gave consent) and sends the order number, total and currency.

```js
analytics.subscribe("checkout_completed", async (event) => {
  const mac = await browser.cookie.get("_adchanger_mac");
  if (!/^[a-z0-9]{12,32}$/.test(mac || "")) return;
  const checkout = event.data.checkout;
  const sale = { kind: "purchase", at: event.timestamp, order_id: String(checkout.order?.id ?? checkout.token) };
  if (["GBP", "USD", "EUR"].includes(checkout.currencyCode)) {
    sale.value_minor = Math.round(Number(checkout.totalPrice.amount) * 100);
    sale.currency = checkout.currencyCode;
  }
  fetch("https://adidmymsbpzrumtytsmg.supabase.co/functions/v1/measure/event", {
    method: "POST",
    keepalive: true,
    headers: { "content-type": "text/plain" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ key: "pk_your_key", mac, events: [sale] }),
  });
});
```

Sales from visitors who did not consent can still be reported from your server, as described next, for example with the discount code on your bar.

## Sales the browser never sees

For sales made by phone, in an app, through a subscription renewal or anywhere the tag cannot run, your server can report the sale directly:

```sh
curl -X POST https://adidmymsbpzrumtytsmg.supabase.co/functions/v1/measure/conversion \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADCHANGER_SECRET_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "idempotency_key": "order-1234",
    "type": "purchase",
    "occurred_at": "2026-10-07T14:30:00Z",
    "click_id": "k3x9q2m7v4p8z1aa",
    "value_minor": 4999,
    "currency": "GBP"
  }'
```

- Authorization: your secret key, which starts with sk_. Keep it on your server only: never put it in a web page, an app or a public repository. If you think it has leaked, email yigit@adchanger.net at once.
- idempotency_key: use the same order number you pass as order_id to adchanger("purchase") on your site (here "order-1234"), so an order reported by both the tag and your server is counted only once. Sending the same key again never counts the sale twice, so a retry is safe.
- occurred_at: when the sale happened, as an ISO 8601 time.
- click_id or discount_code: the click ID (from your own records or the _adchanger_mac cookie), or the discount code on your bar that the customer used. One of the two is required.
- value_minor and currency: the total in minor units (4999 for 49.99) and GBP, USD or EUR.

## Consent and privacy

Without consent, the tag reads the click ID from the page's address and reports what happens during that page view. It stores nothing on the visitor's device and reads nothing from it, so in our understanding it does not need cookie consent under the UK and EU rules on storage (PECR and the ePrivacy Directive). This is not legal advice: you remain responsible for your own consent banner and privacy notice.

Remembering a click across pages and days needs storage, so it needs consent. Only after consent does the tag set one first-party cookie on your domain:

- Name: _adchanger_mac. Value: the click ID and nothing else.
- Lifetime: 7 days, the attribution window. It is set only on the page the click arrived on, so it never extends the window.
- Scope: your site only (first-party, SameSite=Lax, Secure on https).

Tell the tag about consent in one of two ways: add data-consent="granted" to the tag's script element when your consent tool loads it only after consent, or call adchanger("consent", true) when the visitor agrees. If consent is given after the visitor arrived, the click is stored at that moment. Call adchanger("consent", false) when consent is withdrawn and the cookie is deleted.

The tag never uses local storage, never fingerprints a device and never sets third-party cookies.

## What the tag sends

- Always: your site key, the click ID, the kind of event and its time.
- With some events: how many seconds the page was on screen, how far down it was scrolled, and for a sale its order number, value and currency.
- Like any request on the web, the request itself shows our servers (hosted by Supabase) the visitor's IP address and browser; the tag adds nothing more.

The tag never sends names, email addresses, postal addresses, phone numbers, card or bank details, what is on your pages, their addresses, or anything the visitor types.

In the app you see totals only, never individual visitors. How AdChanger handles personal data is set out in the [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy); the advertising side is on [Advertise](https://adchanger.net/advertise).

# Is AdChanger safe?

Source: https://adchanger.net/safety (updated 2026-10-06)

Yes: AdChanger is built to see as little as possible. It asks for no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission, never sees your screen, keystrokes, microphone, camera, app contents or browsing history, and never sees card or bank details, which stay with Whop.

## Who operates AdChanger

AdChanger is operated by its founder, Yiğit Ali Kurt, who is the data controller under UK and EU data protection law and answers personally for how personal data is used.

The one contact address for everything, including privacy requests and complaints, is yigit@adchanger.net.

AdChanger's database runs on Supabase, in London. Whop handles card payments, payouts and ID checks. This website is hosted on GitHub Pages, sets no cookies and runs no analytics.

AdChanger has not launched yet: the Mac app is being built and the download is not public yet.

## Permissions the app asks for, and does not

AdChanger asks for no Screen Recording, Accessibility, Input Monitoring, microphone or camera permission. Without them, macOS does not let an app capture your screen or read what you type in other apps.

The app is built to run inside Apple's App Sandbox. Beyond that, it asks macOS for only two things: to connect to the internet, and to open a file you pick yourself, read-only (such as an advertiser's bar image).

To tell whether your Mac is in use, it asks macOS how many seconds have passed since the last keyboard or mouse input. That number says nothing about which key was pressed or what is on screen.

You can check the permissions yourself on any Mac with AdChanger installed:

- Open System Settings, then Privacy & Security.
- Open Screen & System Audio Recording (called Screen Recording on older versions of macOS): AdChanger is not in the list.
- Open Accessibility, then Input Monitoring: AdChanger is not in either list.
- Open Microphone and Camera: AdChanger is not in those lists either.

On macOS 13 or later, AdChanger adds itself once to the apps that open at login, so the bar keeps its place in the menu bar. You can turn this off in the app's Settings (Open at login) or in System Settings, General, Login Items, and it stays off.

## What data is collected, and what never is

To count a minute, the app only checks that the ad is on screen and that your Mac is awake and in use.

It collects your account details (email, age band, country), a random ID for each Mac, the minutes each ad ran, clicks, and your optional answers about what you do and what you plan to buy. Words you type in your own answers stay on your Mac.

It never collects your screen, keystrokes, microphone or camera, what is inside your apps, your browsing or search history, your contacts, your exact location, a list of your installed apps, or what is on your clipboard.

It never asks about health, medicines, pregnancy, mental health, religion, politics or sexuality.

Advertisers only see totals. They never get your name, your email or a list of people. AdChanger does not sell data or share it with ad networks or data brokers.

The full list, with the legal reason for each item and how long it is kept, is in the [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy).

## How money is handled

- Whop takes advertisers' card payments and sends earners' payouts. AdChanger never sees or stores card or bank details.
- Advertisers pay before a campaign runs. Their budget is set aside in full and spent one verified minute at a time, and they are never charged more than their budget.
- AdChanger's server checks every minute and accepts each one once. Its count is the one that pays, so the same minute cannot be paid twice.
- An earner's share of each minute waits 3 days so invalid activity can be checked, then becomes available to withdraw through Whop.
- Minute, click, payment and earnings records are never edited once written, so the money always adds up.

How much a minute pays, and the full split, is on [Earn on your Mac](https://adchanger.net/earn-money-on-mac) and in the [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms).

## Every ad is reviewed

A person reviews every ad, its link and the page it opens before it runs. An approved ad that is changed is reviewed again.

AdChanger does not accept ads for gambling or betting, adult sexual content or services, prescription medicines, politics or elections, or speculative crypto or token investments.

AdChanger is for people 18 and over, so everyone who sees an ad is an adult. Ads on subjects such as alcohol or dating get a closer look.

Every ad is a still image with a secure https:// link: no animation, no sound and no pop-ups. A link opens only when you click the bar.

## You stay in control

- Pause: click the bar, then Pause. It stays paused until you start it again.
- Snooze: for 1 hour, 3 hours or until tomorrow; the bar comes back on its own.
- Stop: turns the ads off. No minutes count while the bar is paused, snoozed or stopped.
- Your answers: change or clear them in Settings at any time, and switch off "Match the bar to what I'm doing".

Quitting the AdChanger window does not remove the bar: like Wi-Fi, the icon stays in the menu bar while you are logged in. To turn the ads off, press Stop.

To remove AdChanger completely: press Stop, turn off Open at login (in the app's Settings or in System Settings, General, Login Items), log out or restart so the app is no longer running, then move AdChanger from Applications to the Bin.

To close your account, withdraw any available earnings first, then write to yigit@adchanger.net from your account's email address.

## Security practices

- Each person can read only their own records, and each advertiser only their own business's.
- Money, minutes and clicks can only be written by AdChanger's server, never by the app directly.
- AdChanger holds no passwords: you sign in with an email link, Google or GitHub.
- The advertiser pages in the app open only after Touch ID or your Mac's password.
- Staff actions are logged.
- Fake activity (scripts, bots, virtual machines, several accounts) is against the terms, and minutes from it are not paid.

## Your rights and reporting a problem

Under the UK GDPR and the EU GDPR you can ask to see, correct, delete or move your data. Write to yigit@adchanger.net from your account's email; you will get an answer within one month.

To report an ad, a bug or anything that looks wrong, email yigit@adchanger.net. You can also send a bug report from inside the app.

If you are unhappy with how your data is handled, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office in the UK, or to the data protection authority where you live in the EU.

## Questions about safety

### Is AdChanger legit?

AdChanger is an early-access Mac app run by its founder, Yiğit Ali Kurt, reachable at yigit@adchanger.net. Its prices, revenue split, [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms) and [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy) are published, payments and payouts go through Whop, and a person reviews every ad.

### Can AdChanger see my screen?

No. AdChanger asks for no Screen Recording permission, so macOS does not let it capture your screen. You can confirm this in System Settings, Privacy & Security, Screen & System Audio Recording, where AdChanger is not listed.

### Does AdChanger read what I type?

No. AdChanger asks for no Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission and never records keystrokes or what you type in other apps. To know the Mac is in use, it only asks macOS how long ago the last input happened. Words you type in your own answers inside AdChanger stay on your Mac.

### Who pays AdChanger earners, and how?

Advertisers pay for verified minutes, and earners keep their share. Payouts go through Whop: each minute's earnings wait 3 days, then you withdraw to your Whop account and send the money to your bank or card from there. AdChanger never sees your bank details.

### Can I remove AdChanger completely?

Yes. Press Stop, turn off Open at login, log out or restart so the app is no longer running, then move AdChanger from Applications to the Bin. To close your account as well, email yigit@adchanger.net from your account's address.

### Does AdChanger sell my data?

No. AdChanger does not sell data or share it with ad networks or data brokers. Advertisers see only totals, and any group of fewer than 5 people is merged so no one is singled out.

# Frequently asked questions

Source: https://adchanger.net/faq (updated 2026-10-07)

AdChanger is a Mac app that shows one small ad in the menu bar and pays the person who shows it for every verified minute. Advertisers pay £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 verified minutes; the person showing the ad keeps 65%.

## About AdChanger

### What is AdChanger?

AdChanger is a Mac app that puts one small, quiet ad in your menu bar and pays you for every minute it is seen. Businesses use the same app to build the ad, choose who sees it and pay only for verified minutes.

### What is MacAd?

MacAd is the product inside the AdChanger app: one small, still ad in the Mac menu bar, next to the clock. It is AdChanger's first and, so far, only product. There are no pop-ups, no sound and no window to keep open.

### What is a verified minute?

A verified minute is counted after the whole ad has been on screen for 60 seconds while the Mac is awake and in use. AdChanger's server checks every minute and accepts each one once. Advertisers pay for verified minutes and nothing else.

### Who runs AdChanger?

AdChanger is operated by its founder, Yiğit Ali Kurt. The contact address for everything is yigit@adchanger.net. More on the [About](https://adchanger.net/about) page.

### Which Macs does AdChanger work on?

AdChanger works on Macs with macOS 12 Monterey or later. It needs room in the menu bar for one bar, 180 points wide.

### Who can use AdChanger, and where?

Anyone aged 18 or over with a Mac, in any country, can earn; an ad only shows in the countries its advertiser picked. Advertisers can run ads anywhere in the world. The UK is AdChanger's first market.

## Earning

### Can I really get paid to show ads on my Mac?

Yes. AdChanger pays you 65% of what an advertiser pays for each verified minute an ad is seen in your menu bar: £2.60, €3.25 or $3.90 per 1,000 minutes. The download is not public yet.

### How much can I earn with AdChanger?

Advertisers pay £0.004, €0.005 or $0.006 per verified minute and you keep 65%, which is £2.60, €3.25 or $3.90 per 1,000 minutes. As an example, an 8-hour day with an ad running the whole time comes to about £1.25, or roughly £37 over 30 such days. What you really earn depends on the ads running for your country and how long your Mac is in use; no fixed amount is promised.

### Is there a daily limit on AdChanger earnings?

Yes. One person is counted for at most 1,000 minutes of the same ad a day, so one ad can pay you at most £2.60 a day in pounds. Only one of your Macs earns at a time.

### Does AdChanger pay when my Mac is idle or locked?

No. If you are away for 8 minutes, the clock waits. If the Mac locks, sleeps or shuts down, the unfinished minute does not count. AdChanger only pays for time the Mac is awake and in use.

### Do I earn every minute the bar is showing?

Not always. When no paid ad fits you well enough, or during a short break between paid stretches, the bar shows AdChanger's own message, and those minutes earn nothing.

### How does the AdChanger affiliate code work?

If you join with someone's affiliate code, you keep 70% instead of 65%, the code's owner gets 5% and AdChanger keeps 25%. The price the advertiser pays does not change. You can add a code once.

### Can I turn AdChanger off?

Always. Click the bar to pause it, snooze it for 1 hour, 3 hours or until tomorrow, or stop it. No minutes count while it is paused, snoozed or stopped.

### Can I swap AdChanger earnings for a gift code?

Where a brand offers it, adults can swap part of their available earnings for that brand's gift code, worth more than they give. The code can only be used with that brand.

## Payments and payouts

### How do I get paid by AdChanger?

Through Whop. Each minute's earnings wait 3 days, then you can withdraw from £10, €10 or $10, one withdrawal at a time. Whop checks your ID once and holds your bank details; AdChanger never sees them.

### Why are AdChanger earnings held for a few days?

Each minute's earnings wait 3 days so invalid activity, such as scripts or fake accounts, can be checked before money is paid out. After that they become available to withdraw.

### Are there fees on AdChanger payouts?

The terms set out no charge for earning. When you send money from Whop to your bank or card, Whop's own terms and fees apply, and they come out of the amount you send.

### Which payment methods does AdChanger support?

Whop, for now, for both advertiser payments and earner payouts. Stripe, Wise and PayPal are planned.

### Do I pay tax on AdChanger earnings?

You are responsible for any tax on what you earn through AdChanger. The rules depend on where you live.

### Where does each minute's money go?

Of every verified minute, 65% goes to the person showing the ad and 35% to AdChanger. With an affiliate code, it is 70% to the earner, 5% to the code's owner and 25% to AdChanger.

## Privacy and safety

### Is AdChanger safe?

AdChanger is built to see as little as possible. To count a minute it only checks that the ad is on screen and that your Mac is awake and in use, and it asks for no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission. A person reviews every ad. The details are on [Is AdChanger safe?](https://adchanger.net/safety).

### Is AdChanger legit?

AdChanger names its operator (Yiğit Ali Kurt), gives a contact address (yigit@adchanger.net), and publishes its prices, revenue split, [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms) and [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy). Money moves through Whop, so AdChanger never sees card or bank details.

### What does AdChanger never see?

Your screen, what you type, your microphone or camera, what is inside your apps, your browsing or search history, your contacts, your exact location or your clipboard.

### How does AdChanger choose which ad I see?

From your optional answers (what you do on your Mac, your interests, what you plan to buy) and the app in front of you right now. The name of that app never leaves your Mac, and you can switch this matching off in Settings.

### What do advertisers learn about me from AdChanger?

Nothing that identifies you. Advertisers see totals only, and any group of fewer than 5 people is merged so no one is singled out. They never get your name, email, Mac or answers.

### Does the AdChanger website use cookies?

No. adchanger.net sets no cookies, uses no local storage and runs no analytics or tracking. Advertisers who add the AdChanger tag to their own sites may set one cookie there, only with your consent, holding just the click ID for 7 days ([how it works](https://adchanger.net/measure)).

### Can under-18s use AdChanger?

No. AdChanger is for people 18 and over, and Whop checks your ID before your first payout.

## Advertising

### How much does it cost to advertise with MacAd?

£4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 verified minutes, depending on your billing currency. You pay nothing for unfinished minutes or idle screens. More on [Advertise](https://adchanger.net/advertise).

### How do advertisers pay AdChanger?

Through Whop, before a campaign runs: each payment is between 10 and 10,000 in your currency. Whop takes the card and AdChanger never sees it. Budget you do not spend stays as credit for your next campaign.

### Who sees a MacAd bar?

People whose Mac fits the campaign: the countries and cities chosen, what they do on their Mac, their interests and buying plans, and the app in front of them at that moment. If nothing fits well enough, no paid bar shows.

### What do advertisers see in their results?

Verified minutes and spend, then how many people saw the bar, noticed it, clicked it, reached the advertiser's page and became customers. A sale counts when it happens within 7 days of a click, and groups of fewer than 5 people are merged.

### Is every ad allowed on AdChanger?

No. A person reviews every ad, its link and its page before it runs. Gambling, adult content, prescription medicines, politics and speculative crypto investments are not accepted, and adult-only products are never shown to under-18s.

## Waitlist

### When can I download AdChanger?

Soon. The Mac app is being built and the download is not public yet. It will be on the [home page](https://adchanger.net/) the day it is ready.

### How do I join the AdChanger waitlist?

Email yigit@adchanger.net with the subject "Waitlist", saying whether you want to earn or advertise. The buttons on this website open that email for you. There is nothing to download yet: you get an email when the download is ready.

### Will everything work from the first day?

Features may change, pause or not be switched on yet, including payouts. The [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms) are kept up to date as that happens.

# About AdChanger

Source: https://adchanger.net/about (updated 2026-10-07)

AdChanger is a bootstrapped advertising startup founded in September 2026 by Yiğit Ali Kurt. Its working pre-launch native macOS app creates a new menu-bar advertising surface, with the UK as its first market.

## What AdChanger is

AdChanger is one Mac app with two sides. People with a Mac use it to show one small, still ad in their menu bar and earn from it. Businesses use the same app to build that ad, choose who sees it and pay for the minutes it is seen.

MacAd is the product inside the app: the ad in the menu bar, next to the clock. It is AdChanger's first product and, so far, its only one.

## Why it exists

People's attention already pays for advertising. Every ad someone sees is paid for by a business, and that money goes to whoever sells the space, not to the person looking.

AdChanger shares it. An advertiser pays £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 verified minutes, and the person whose Mac shows the ad keeps 65% of every minute. AdChanger keeps 35%.

For businesses, the same rule means paying only for minutes an ad was really on screen in front of someone using their Mac, never for an idle screen.

## Principles

- Pay per verified minute: a minute counts after 60 seconds fully on screen while the Mac is awake and in use, and the server accepts each minute once.
- See almost nothing: the app never sees the screen, keystrokes, microphone, camera, app contents or browsing history, and asks for no Screen Recording or Accessibility permission.
- People in control: the bar can be paused, snoozed or stopped at any time, and answers about yourself are optional.
- Every ad reviewed: a person checks every ad, its link and its page before it runs.
- Numbers published: the price of a minute, the split and the payout rules are on this website and in the [terms](https://adchanger.net/terms).

## Who runs it

AdChanger is operated by its founder, Yiğit Ali Kurt, who is the data controller for the personal data described in the [privacy notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy) and the party to the [terms of use](https://adchanger.net/terms).

AdChanger's database runs on Supabase in London. Whop handles card payments, payouts and ID checks, so AdChanger never sees card or bank details. This website is hosted on GitHub Pages and sets no cookies.

## Where it stands

AdChanger is pre-launch. The native Mac app, campaign builder, serving stack and measurement foundation are working, but the public download is not live yet and the first live advertiser pilots are still ahead.

The UK is the first market, with prices in pounds first (£4 per 1,000 verified minutes). Anyone with a Mac, in any country, can earn, and advertisers can run ads anywhere in the world.

To join the waitlist, email yigit@adchanger.net. How earning works is on [Earn on your Mac](https://adchanger.net/earn-money-on-mac), advertising on [Advertise](https://adchanger.net/advertise), and safety on [Is AdChanger safe?](https://adchanger.net/safety). Common questions are answered in the [FAQ](https://adchanger.net/faq).

## Contact

yigit@adchanger.net is the one address for everything: the waitlist, advertising, privacy requests, reports and press.

# Privacy Notice

Source: https://adchanger.net/privacy (updated 2026-10-07)

This Privacy Notice explains what personal data AdChanger collects, why it is collected, with whom it is shared, how long it is kept and the rights available to you.

## 1. Who we are

AdChanger (“AdChanger”, “we”, “us” or “our”) is operated by Yiğit Ali Kurt, who is the data controller for the personal data described in this notice. As data controller, he determines how and why that personal data is used and is responsible for it under applicable data protection law.

You may contact us about any matter in this notice at yigit@adchanger.net.

## 2. Scope

This notice applies to the AdChanger Mac application (the “app”), including MacAd, the advertisement displayed in the Mac menu bar (the “bar”), and to our website, adchanger.net (together, the “Service”).

It applies to individuals who display advertisements through the app and earn from them (“Earners”) and to businesses, and the people acting for them, that run advertisements through the Service (“Advertisers”).

This notice should be read together with our [Terms of Use](https://adchanger.net/terms), which govern your use of the Service.

## 3. Summary

The Service is designed to process as little personal data as possible. In summary:

- The app never accesses your screen, your keystrokes, your microphone or camera, the contents of your applications or your browsing history.
- To count a minute, the app checks only that the advertisement is on screen and that your Mac is awake and in use.
- Information you provide about yourself is optional. It is stored as fixed choices from a predefined list; any words you type yourself remain on your Mac.
- Advertisers receive aggregated totals only. They never receive your name, your email address or a list of individuals.
- We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it with advertising networks or data brokers.
- Our website sets no cookies and runs no analytics. Advertisers who use the AdChanger tag on their own websites may, with your consent, set one cookie there that holds only a click identifier for 7 days (section 5.5).

## 4. Information we never collect

The app does not collect, and is not designed to access, any of the following:

- Your screen, screenshots or screen recordings. The app does not request screen-recording permission.
- Your keystrokes or anything you type in other applications. The app does not request Accessibility permission.
- Your microphone or camera.
- The contents of your applications, documents or messages.
- Your browsing or search history.
- Your contacts, your precise location or a list of the applications installed on your Mac.
- Your clipboard. When you open a bar that includes a discount code, the app copies that code to your clipboard for your convenience; it never reads the contents of your clipboard.
- Information about your health, medicines, pregnancy, mental health, religion, political opinions or sexuality. We never ask for this information.

## 5. Information we collect and why

For each category of personal data below, we set out the purpose for which we use it and the legal basis on which we rely under the UK General Data Protection Regulation (“UK GDPR”) and the EU General Data Protection Regulation (“EU GDPR”).

### 5.1 Account information

Your email address and, if you sign in with Google or GitHub, the basic profile information that service provides, such as your name. We also record that you confirmed you are 18 or over, the date you joined and your country. Your country is derived from the network connection your Mac uses or, where that is not available, from your Mac’s region setting. We do not store your IP address in our database.

Purpose: to operate your account, protect your earnings and apply the age rules described in section 11. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you.

### 5.2 Device information

A randomly generated identifier for each Mac on which you use AdChanger, the app version and the macOS version. We collect no other information about your hardware.

Purpose: to identify which Mac is earning (only one Mac per person may earn at a time) and to diagnose problems. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you, and our legitimate interest in preventing fraud.

### 5.3 Minutes and use of the bar

For each minute an advertisement is displayed: which advertisement it was, when the minute started and ended, and how many times your pointer rested on the bar (which we refer to as “noticed”). We also record when you start, pause, snooze or stop the bar, when you open its window, when the bar is covered or has no room in the menu bar, how long the pointer rested on it, and actions such as selecting “Not for me”.

Purpose: to count verified minutes, pay Earners, charge Advertisers correctly, detect invalid activity and provide Advertisers with accurate totals. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you, and our legitimate interests in preventing fraud and measuring results.

### 5.4 Clicks

When you click a bar, we record the click and assign it a random identifier. The Advertiser’s link then opens with that identifier added (as the parameter mac=) so that a sale can be matched to the bar. Any processing on the Advertiser’s own website is governed by that Advertiser’s privacy notice.

Purpose: to allow Advertisers to pay for results they can verify, and to show you the advertisements you have clicked. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you, and our legitimate interests.

### 5.5 The AdChanger tag on Advertisers’ websites

An Advertiser may add the AdChanger tag to its own website. If you arrive there from a bar, the tag sends us the click identifier from the page address, the kind of event (arriving, viewing the page for 30 seconds, scrolling or viewing a second page, adding to a basket, purchasing), when it happened, how long the page was viewed and how far it was scrolled, and, for a purchase, the Advertiser’s order number, the order value and its currency. As with any request on the internet, our servers also receive your IP address and browser details when the tag sends this information. The tag sends nothing if you did not arrive from a bar.

The tag stores nothing on your device unless the Advertiser’s website has obtained your consent. Only then does it set one first-party cookie, named _adchanger_mac, on the Advertiser’s website. It holds the click identifier and nothing else, expires after 7 days and is deleted if you withdraw your consent. The tag does not use local storage, fingerprinting or third-party cookies, and it never sends your name, email address, postal address, payment details, the contents or addresses of the pages you view, or anything you type.

An Advertiser may also report a sale to us from its own systems, identified by the click identifier or by the discount code shown in its bar, together with the order value and currency.

Purpose: to tell an Advertiser how many clicks on its bar led to visits and sales, within 7 days of the click. Legal basis: our legitimate interest, and that of Advertisers, in measuring the results of advertising. Consent for the cookie is collected by the Advertiser’s website, and the Advertiser’s own privacy notice also applies there. Advertisers see these results only as totals.

### 5.6 Your answers (optional)

Information you choose to provide about what you do on your Mac, your interests, what you plan to buy, life events such as moving house, and subjects on which you never wish to see advertisements. These answers are sent as fixed choices from our predefined list. Any words you type in your own answers remain on your Mac. Purchase plans carry less weight after 60 days and cease to be taken into account after 120 days.

Purpose: to show you advertisements that are relevant to you. Legal basis: your consent. Providing answers is optional, and you may change or clear them in Settings at any time.

### 5.7 The application in use (the “moment”)

On your Mac, the app checks which application you are currently using, for example a coding tool or a design tool, so that it can select a bar that fits. The identity of that application never leaves your Mac. Our server receives only two yes-or-no values: whether the moment was used to select the bar, and whether the selected bar matched it. One selection in five deliberately leaves the moment out, so that we can measure whether it improves relevance.

Purpose: to select a bar suited to what you are doing and to measure whether doing so helps. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in showing relevant advertisements. You may switch this off in Settings under “Match the bar to what I’m doing”.

### 5.8 Learning on your Mac

While your answers are in use, the app also learns from your interactions with its own bar: which bars you rest on, open, click or pass over. This information remains on your Mac, carries half as much weight every 30 days and is erased when you clear your answers. It never relates to anything outside AdChanger’s own bar.

Purpose: to refine which bars are shown to you. Legal basis: this processing takes place only on your Mac and only while your answers, which rely on your consent, are in use; it ends when you clear them.

### 5.9 Earnings and payouts

The amount you earned each minute, the amounts pending and available, your withdrawals and the identifier of your Whop account. If you use an affiliate code, which code you used and when. We never see or store your bank or card details; Whop holds them.

Purpose: to pay you the correct amount, exactly once. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you, and our legal obligation to keep financial records.

### 5.10 Advertiser information

The business name, website and billing country; the permissions of each member of the Advertiser’s team; Campaigns, bar images, links, discount codes, budgets and review decisions; and the amount and Whop reference of each payment. Card details are provided to Whop and never to us. If an Advertiser offers gift codes to Earners, we keep those codes confidential until an Earner exchanges earnings for one.

Purpose: to operate Advertiser accounts and Campaigns and to record payments. Legal basis: performance of our contract with the Advertiser, and our legal obligation to keep financial records.

### 5.11 Bug reports and correspondence

If you submit a bug report from the app, we receive what you write and any screenshots or videos you choose to attach. If you email us, we receive your message and your email address.

Purpose: to resolve problems and respond to you. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in fixing problems and answering your enquiries.

## 6. What Advertisers can see

- Aggregated totals: verified minutes, spend, and the number of people who saw, noticed and clicked the bar, reached the Advertiser’s page and became customers.
- Results by location and time are grouped. Any group of fewer than 5 people is merged into “other”, so that no individual can be singled out.
- Audience estimates shown while an Advertiser plans a Campaign are rounded and are hidden below the same threshold.
- Advertisers never see your name, email address, Mac, answers or any list of individuals.

## 7. Service providers

We use a limited number of service providers to operate the Service. Each receives only the personal data it needs to perform its function.

- Supabase: our database, sign-in, file storage and server code. Our database is located in London.
- Whop: Advertiser card payments, Earner payouts and the identity check Whop requires before it makes a payout. Whop’s own privacy policy applies to information you provide to Whop directly.
- Google and GitHub: only if you choose to sign in with either of them.
- Google Workspace: our email, including messages you send to us.
- GitHub (GitHub Pages): hosting of our website.

The selection of the advertisements you see takes place in our own database and on your Mac. No third party receives your answers. Should we in future use an external tool to improve how advertisements are selected, it will receive only data that contains no names, email addresses, typed words, IP addresses or payment details.

## 8. International transfers

Our database is located in the United Kingdom. Some of the service providers listed in section 7, such as Whop, Google and GitHub, are based in the United States and may process personal data there. Where personal data is transferred outside the United Kingdom or the European Economic Area, we rely on the safeguards those providers offer for such transfers. You may contact us for further information.

## 9. Retention

- Your answers are kept until you change or clear them or close your account. Purchase plans cease to be taken into account after 120 days.
- What the app learns on your Mac carries half as much weight every 30 days and is erased when you clear your answers.
- Records of minutes, clicks, payments and earnings are never altered once written, so that all amounts reconcile. We retain them after an account is closed because we require them for accounting and tax purposes.
- When you close your account, we delete your answers and anything derived from them, disconnect your Macs and remove your name and city. Your email address and financial records remain associated with the closed account.
- We have not yet set fixed periods after which closed accounts are deleted in full. When we do, we will publish them in this notice.

## 10. Your rights

Under the UK GDPR and the EU GDPR, you have the right to request access to the personal data we hold about you and a copy of it; to have it corrected; to have it erased; to restrict or object to its use; and to have it transferred to another service. Where we rely on your consent, you may withdraw it at any time. Where we rely on legitimate interests, you may object to that processing.

To exercise any of these rights, please write to yigit@adchanger.net from the email address associated with your account. We will respond within one month. Some actions are available to you directly in the app: you may change or clear your answers, switch off matching to the application in use, and pause, snooze or stop the bar.

If you are dissatisfied with how we handle your personal data, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioner’s Office (ico.org.uk) in the United Kingdom, or with the data protection authority in your country of residence in the European Union. We would, however, welcome the opportunity to address your concerns first.

## 11. Age

- AdChanger is for people 18 or older. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone younger; if we learn that an account belongs to someone under 18, we close it and delete their answers.
- Whop verifies your identity before your first payout.
- You may switch off the use of your answers in Settings at any time. While they are off, you are shown no advertisements and earn nothing, because advertisers pay for advertisements matched to people.

## 12. Security

Each person can access only their own records, and each Advertiser only the records of its own business. Money, minutes and clicks can be written only by our server, never directly by the app. We hold no passwords: you sign in with an email link, Google or GitHub. The Advertiser sections of the app open only after Touch ID or your Mac’s password. Actions taken by staff are logged.

Further information is available on our [security and safety page](https://adchanger.net/safety).

## 13. Cookies and similar technologies

Our website sets no cookies, uses no local storage and runs no analytics or tracking. As with any web host, GitHub receives your IP address and browser details when it delivers a page to you. The download and email buttons open your own email application; nothing is sent until you choose to send it.

The AdChanger tag that Advertisers may add to their own websites is described in section 5.5. It sets a cookie only on the Advertiser’s website, only after you consent there, and only for 7 days; it never sets a cookie on adchanger.net.

## 14. Changes to this notice

The AdChanger app is in a pre-release stage, and the Service will change over time. When this notice changes, we will update the “Last updated” date at the top. If a change affects how we use your personal data, we will inform you in the app or by email before it takes effect.

## 15. Contact

Questions, requests and complaints about this notice may be sent to yigit@adchanger.net.

# Terms of Use

Source: https://adchanger.net/terms (updated 2026-10-06)

These Terms of Use set out the conditions on which Earners and Advertisers may use AdChanger and MacAd.

## 1. Introduction and acceptance

These Terms of Use (the “Terms”) form an agreement between you and Yiğit Ali Kurt, trading as AdChanger (“AdChanger”, “we”, “us” or “our”).

AdChanger is a Mac application. MacAd is the product within it: a single advertisement displayed in the Mac menu bar (the “bar”). By using the app, you agree to these Terms. Our [Privacy Notice](https://adchanger.net/privacy) explains how we handle your personal data.

The AdChanger app is in a pre-release stage and is not yet publicly available for download. Certain features, including payouts, may be introduced, changed or suspended, or may not yet be enabled. We will keep these Terms up to date as this happens, and we encourage you to report anything that appears to be incorrect.

## 2. Definitions

In these Terms, the following words have the meanings given below:

- “Account” means the account you hold with AdChanger, through which you use the app as an Earner, an Advertiser or both.
- “Advertiser” means a business that runs advertisements through AdChanger, and the person acting for it.
- “Campaign” means an Advertiser’s advertisement, together with its link, budget and settings, as submitted for display in the bar.
- “Credit” means money an Advertiser has added to its Account through Whop, from which Campaign budgets are set aside.
- “Earner” means a person who displays advertisements in the menu bar of their Mac through the app and earns from Verified minutes.
- “Verified minute” means a minute of display that meets the counting rules in section 4.2 and has been accepted by our server.
- “Whop” means the third-party service through which Advertisers make payments and Earners receive payouts.

## 3. Eligibility and accounts

- You must be 18 or older to use AdChanger, and you confirm this when you start. Whop verifies your identity before your first payout.
- Anyone with a Mac, in any country, may earn. An advertisement is shown only in the countries its Advertiser has selected, so the advertisements available to you depend on where you are.
- To advertise, you must be authorised to act for the business you advertise.
- Each person may hold one Account. You must keep access to your email and sign-in method secure, and you are responsible for activity on your Account.

## 4. Terms for Earners

### 4.1 The bar

MacAd displays one advertisement at a time in your menu bar. You may pause, snooze or stop it at any time. The bar may sometimes display a message from AdChanger instead of a paid advertisement, for example when no advertisement is sufficiently suited to you or during a short break between periods of paid display. No earnings accrue for those minutes.

### 4.2 How a Verified minute is counted

- A minute counts once the whole advertisement has been on screen for 60 seconds while your Mac is awake and in use.
- If you are away from your Mac for 8 minutes, the count pauses. The count also pauses if the bar is covered or has no room in the menu bar.
- If your Mac locks, sleeps or shuts down, or you pause, snooze or stop the bar, the unfinished minute does not count.
- Our server checks every minute and accepts each minute only once. The server’s count is the count on which payment is based.

### 4.3 Earnings

Advertisers pay £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 Verified minutes, depending on their currency. You receive 65% of the price of each Verified minute you display, and AdChanger retains 35%. If you joined using another person’s affiliate code, you receive 70%, the code’s owner receives 5% and AdChanger retains 25%. Shares are rounded down to the smallest unit we record.

- A person is counted for no more than 1,000 minutes of the same advertisement per day.
- Only one of your Macs may earn at a time.
- You do not earn from advertisements run by your own business.
- We do not guarantee any level of earnings. What you earn depends on the advertisements running where you are and on how long your Mac is in use.

### 4.4 Payouts

- The earnings for each minute are held for 3 days so that we can check for invalid activity, after which they become available.
- You may withdraw available earnings of £10, €10 or $10 or more, one withdrawal at a time.
- Payouts are made through Whop. You link a Whop account, and Whop verifies your identity once. You then transfer the money from Whop to your bank account or card on Whop’s website.
- Whop’s own terms and fees apply to that transfer, and Whop’s fees are deducted from the amount you transfer.
- You are responsible for any tax due on your earnings.

### 4.5 Affiliate codes

You may add another person’s affiliate code once. While the code is active, you receive 70% and its owner receives 5% of the price of your Verified minutes. If you remove the code, you continue to receive 70%, the 5% passes to AdChanger, and you may not add a code again. The price Advertisers pay is unaffected.

### 4.6 Exchanging earnings for gift codes

Where a brand offers it, Earners may exchange part of their available earnings for that brand’s gift code, which is worth more than the amount exchanged. The amount is deducted from your balance immediately. The gift code is issued by the brand, may be used only with that brand and is subject to the brand’s terms.

## 5. Invalid activity

We pay only for genuine use of a Mac by a real person. You must not:

- use scripts, bots, virtual machines or any other means to simulate activity;
- modify the app, its clock or its communications with our server, or replay minutes;
- operate more than one Account, or share one Account between several people;
- click your own advertisements, or advertisements in which you have no genuine interest, or ask others to do so; or
- conceal your location in order to receive advertisements intended for another country.

Where we detect signs of such activity, the affected minutes may not count, earnings may be held while we investigate, amounts paid for invalid minutes may be reclaimed, and the Account may be closed. Where we are able to, we will tell you the reason and give you an opportunity to respond.

## 6. Terms for Advertisers

### 6.1 Business account and currency

You set your business’s billing country once, before your first payment. It determines your currency: pounds sterling in the United Kingdom, euros in the European Union and US dollars elsewhere. Prices are £4, €5 or $6 per 1,000 Verified minutes in those respective currencies.

### 6.2 Advertisement content and review

- You are responsible for your advertisement, its link and the page it opens. You must hold the rights to every word, logo and image it contains, and its content must be accurate.
- The advertisement must be a still image (without animation), at the size specified in the app, with a secure https:// link.
- A person reviews every advertisement, its link and the page it opens before it runs. We may approve it, request changes or reject it, and we will tell you the reason.
- Any change to an approved advertisement is reviewed again before it runs.
- We may stop a running advertisement if it breaches these Terms or the law.

### 6.3 Prohibited categories

We do not accept advertisements for:

- gambling or betting;
- adult sexual content or services;
- prescription medicines;
- politics or elections; or
- speculative cryptocurrency or token investments.

Advertisements on sensitive subjects, such as alcohol or dating, receive closer scrutiny during review.

### 6.4 Payment and budgets

- You add funds through Whop before a Campaign runs. Whop processes your card, and we never see your card details. Each payment must be between 10 and 10,000 in your currency.
- The funds become your Credit. A Campaign’s budget is set aside from your Credit in full before the Campaign starts.
- The budget is spent one Verified minute at a time. When it is exhausted, the bar stops displaying the Campaign. You are never charged more than your budget.
- You are not charged for unfinished minutes, for any period during which an Earner has paused, snoozed or stopped the bar, or while your Campaign is not running.
- If, through our error, a minute is displayed beyond your budget, you are not charged for it.

### 6.5 Unused budget and refunds

Unspent budget is returned to your Credit for use in future Campaigns. Unused Credit is not refundable in cash, with one exception: if we reject your advertisement and not a single minute of it has run, we will refund the corresponding payment. This does not affect any rights you have under applicable law.

### 6.6 Results and attribution

You receive aggregated totals: Verified minutes, spend, and the number of people who saw, noticed and clicked your advertisement, reached your page and became customers. Groups of fewer than 5 people are merged so that no individual can be singled out, and you never receive a list of individuals. A sale is attributed to your advertisement when it occurs within 7 days of a click on it.

If your advertisement includes a discount code, you must honour it. If you report sales to us from your website or shop, you are responsible for informing your visitors in your own privacy notice.

### 6.7 Gift-code offers

You may offer Earners your own gift codes in exchange for part of their earnings. The amount an Earner exchanges is added to your Credit for future Campaigns. You must honour every gift code you provide to us.

## 7. Acceptable use

All users of AdChanger must comply with the following:

- You must not use AdChanger to break the law, or to harm, mislead or send unsolicited messages to anyone.
- You must not attempt to gain access to other people’s Accounts or data, or to our systems.
- You must not copy, reverse engineer or resell the app, except to the extent permitted by law.
- You must not overload or disrupt the Service.

The AdChanger app, MacAd and the adchanger.net website belong to AdChanger. These Terms permit you to use them as described here and do not transfer any ownership to you.

Advertisers retain all rights in their advertisements. By submitting a Campaign, an Advertiser permits AdChanger to display the advertisement, and to use it as needed to review and run the Campaign, for the duration of that Campaign.

## 9. Availability and disclaimers

We aim to keep AdChanger available and to count every minute accurately. However, as the Service is in a pre-release stage, we do not guarantee that it will always be available, that a paid advertisement will always be displayed, or that an advertisement will reach a particular number of people or achieve a particular result.

Further information about how we protect the Service and its users is available on our [security and safety page](https://adchanger.net/safety).

## 10. Limitation of liability

Nothing in these Terms limits our liability where the law does not permit it to be limited, such as for fraud or for death or personal injury caused by negligence. Subject to that, and to the extent permitted by law, we are not liable for losses that we could not reasonably have foreseen, or for loss of profits, business or opportunities.

## 11. Suspension and termination

- You may stop the bar, or stop using AdChanger, at any time.
- To close your Account, write to yigit@adchanger.net from the email address associated with your Account. Please withdraw any available earnings first.
- If you have Advertiser Credit remaining when you wish to close your Account, please contact us first.
- We may suspend or close an Account that breaches these Terms, puts others at risk or is used for invalid activity. Where we are able to, we will tell you the reason.
- Records of minutes, payments and earnings are retained after an Account is closed, as explained in our Privacy Notice.

## 12. Changes to these Terms

When these Terms change, we will update the “Last updated” date at the top. If a change materially affects you, we will inform you in the app or by email before it takes effect. A change in price applies only to minutes displayed after it takes effect; minutes already displayed retain their original price.

## 13. Notices and contact

Questions and notices concerning these Terms may be sent to yigit@adchanger.net.
